title: security in an editor is the editor's chapter, and the security chapter is the running language's
scope:
where a rule about concealing a `secret` on screen lives, and the test that decides it. The
rules themselves are unchanged in substance; what changes is which chapter owns them, and therefore

summary.headline: A rule about what the editor draws belongs to the editor chapter
summary.body:
The rulebook's security chapter holds only rules that still hold with no editor running: what
the compiler refuses, what a running program can reach. Rules about blurring a secret on screen,
the editor's dependency allowlist or which server version a client accepts moved to the editor
chapter, where they sit together as one section on security in the editor. No rule was weakened
or changed; five rules changed address so that a reader of the ground rules can tell a compiler
guarantee from an editor convenience.
